Variants.Content: Ironoaks is the seat of House Waynwood, a powerful vassal house of the Vale. Its name joins hard iron with deep-rooted oak, fitting the ideal of the Vale's nobility: land should be steady, a house enduring, and oaths able to stand firm in the mountain wind. The Waynwood lands link the interior of the Vale, valley roads, and the complex terrain near the High Road, enjoying the bounty of fertile plains while remaining on guard against mountain clans and severed roads. Noble life here cannot be separated from knights, squires, marriage alliances, and courtly custom, yet once winter comes or the mountain paths grow restless, bringing in grain and holding the passes matter more than ceremony.
Entry Ironoaks Local families also rely on goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains; if any road, well, or dock fails, the price falls first on them.

Entry Ironoaks They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the valley; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Ironoaks If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

From workshops to sanctuaries, Ironoaks sets stone walls, wooden beams, iron gates, crypts, and the seams left by generations of repairs side by side with chapels of the Seven, the threat of the mountain clans, and Andal knightly tradition. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Ironoaks They care about goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
